question.problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & b & c\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $a=0,$ $b=\frac{1}{2},$ $c=-\frac{3}{2}$ and 

$$
a+b+c=0+\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{3}{2})=-1.
$$
